meta.title: Three Assemblies, One AND Gate
meta.subtitle: Our own asmdefs — and the seven-input AND that deletes an entire assembly without printing anything

views.label: Packages become symbols
views.note: A version define says: if that package exists, define this symbol — for this one assembly only.

views.label: Why three and not one
views.note: Editor-only code cannot be referenced from runtime code, or the reference silently drops in a build.

views.label: The silent death
views.note: One unsatisfied symbol and the whole assembly is skipped. No DLL, no warning, no error.

boundaries.label: one DLL each · references point upward · nothing runtime may reach down

cards.title: The trap, stated once
items: The constraint list is an AND across every symbol in it
One symbol undefined and Unity skips the assembly entirely, not partially
There is no error, no warning, and no DLL — the types simply cease to exist
What you see instead is a type-not-found error in your own file, which sends you hunting in the wrong place

cards.title: The seven symbols our assemblies demand
items: Two for the BovineLabs graph packages, canopy and grove
Three for Unity services: core, authentication, analytics
One for the platform toolkit — and the authoring assembly adds the editor symbol on top

cards.title: Why the split is three and not one
items: Runtime code referencing an editor-only assembly compiles fine in the editor
In a player build that assembly does not exist and the reference silently drops
So it cannot fail until the first build, where it looks like a catastrophic regression
Three assemblies make the boundary a compile error instead of a build-day surprise

cards.title: The only honest check
items: List the script assemblies folder and look for the DLL by name
All three of ours are there: runtime, authoring, editor
If one is missing, its constraints failed — read them before reading your code
Symbols are per assembly, so every asmdef must declare its own version defines
